**Step 1: Payment formula**

For a principal $P=\$50{,}000$, monthly rate $r=\text{APR}/12$, and $n$ monthly payments:

$$\text{PMT}=P\frac{r(1+r)^n}{(1+r)^n-1}$$

$$\text{Total cost of borrowing}=n(\text{PMT})-P+\text{fee}$$

The upfront fee for Loans A and B is $0.03(\$50{,}000)=\$1{,}500$.

**Step 2: Calculate each loan**

- **Loan A:** $r=0.059/12=0.0049167$, $n=72$  
  $\text{PMT}\approx \$826.29$  
  Total payments $\approx \$59{,}492.61$; interest $\approx \$9{,}492.61$  
  Total cost $= \$9{,}492.61+\$1{,}500.00 = \$10{,}992.61$

- **Loan B:** $r=0.059/12=0.0049167$, $n=60$  
  $\text{PMT}\approx \$964.32$  
  Total payments $\approx \$57{,}859.01$; interest $\approx \$7{,}859.01$  
  Total cost $= \$7{,}859.01+\$1{,}500.00 = \$9{,}359.01$

- **Loan C:** $r=0.089/12=0.0074167$, $n=72$  
  $\text{PMT}\approx \$898.80$  
  Total payments $\approx \$64{,}713.40$; interest $\approx \$14{,}713.40$  
  Total cost $= \$14{,}713.40+\$0 = \$14{,}713.40$

**Step 3: Compare**

$\$9{,}359.01 \;(\text{B}) < \$10{,}992.61 \;(\text{A}) < \$14{,}713.40 \;(\text{C})$

Loan **B** has the lowest total cost of borrowing.
